original.target_description: Unassigned side/fields: placeholders only; do not overwrite previously verified fields.

replication.target_description: Hull et al. (2002), Study 1b: elderly versus neutral scrambled-sentence priming, walking time, and private self-consciousness. Narrative discussion explicitly covers both Studies 1a and 1b. No new effect-size or p extraction is assigned.

n.location: p. 408 (PDF p. 3), Participants—Study 1b; p. 409 (PDF p. 4), Procedure—Study 1b and Results—Study 1b
n.quote: Forty pedestrians were stopped on a central, grassy area in ... the local community and asked to participate in a class project. ... Participants ... who did not proceed directly down the walkway without stopping were ... excluded from the study.
n.sample_role: Participants: final analytic number for Study 1b walking-time ANOVA not explicitly established; 40 is a recruitment count only.
n.exclusions: Only pedestrians appearing under 50 were approached. Those not proceeding directly down the walkway without stopping were excluded; number excluded is not stated.

reported_success.location: p. 409 (PDF p. 4), Studies 1a and 1b—Discussion, opening paragraph
reported_success.quote: Across two studies, individuals who were high in private self- ... consciousness but not those who were low in self-consciousness ... showed greater responsivity to a manipulation that is typically ... interpreted as affecting behavior in an automatic fashion.

notes: Only assigned unfinished fields are completed. All other fields are placeholders. The narrative verdict is coded mixed because the authors explicitly describe greater prime responsiveness for high but not low self-conscious participants; this is a conditional author conclusion, not a verdict inferred from p values. The combined-analysis statement that the prime effect replicates Bargh et al. is not treated as a separate-study unconditional verdict. Target-match identifies the study/outcome supporting assigned fields only, not any unassigned statistic. Study 1b explicitly reports forty pedestrians at recruitment and a behavioral exclusion rule, but no final analytic count or mutually exclusive final group counts. No N is inferred from F(1, 36). Combined-study correlation Ns 36 and 32 refer to prime conditions pooled across studies and cannot establish Study 1b N. No N sum is performed.
